subject: How can I use or set an unlinked marker as a cofactor for MQM?

messages.author: 785a622478f1871a
messages.subject: How can I use or set an unlinked marker as a cofactor for MQM?
parts:
Question:

I have an unlinked marker that I need to use as a cofactor or covariate for MQM.

I know that this marker accounts for a large amount of phenotypic variance for multiple end-use quality traits that I'm looking at in a standard bi-parental mapping population with 132 RILs.

For one phenotype of interest, for example, when a one way ANOVA test was calculated for single marker trait associations this marker was the most significant out of all of the 600 markers that were tested.

How do I account for this single, unlinked locus in my model for MQM?

I was thinking that I might be able to assign this locus as a cofactor but again it's unlinked.

Any help or advice would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Jeff

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How can I use or set an unlinked marker as a cofactor for MQM?
parts:
I think you can use mqmsetcofactors().
See page 12 of the MQM tutorial: http://rqtl.org/tutorials/MQM-tour.pdf

karl

messages.author: 92292fc48bf46044
messages.subject: Re: How can I use or set an unlinked marker as a cofactor for MQM?
parts:
You could just update the list of cofactors, which is simply a vector of 1's and 0's, specifying which markers should be included as cofactor.

If this doesn't work (since MQM does have some issues with single marker chromosomes (e.g. unlinked markers), I would just compensate/ adjust the phenotype for the marker in question, and then use the adjusted phenotype for further (multiple) QTL mapping

Danny
